# Amazon Redshift auto-copy from Amazon S3

## Overview

An auto-copy job loads data into Amazon Redshift tables from files stored in Amazon S3. Amazon Redshift detects new S3 files added to the path specified in the COPY command, and a COPY command is run automatically when new files are detected. Redshift keeps track of which files have been loaded and determines the number of files batched per COPY command. A COPY JOB is defined once, and the same parameters are used for future runs. Defining and managing a COPY JOB requires permission.

## Creating the S3 event integration

The first step in creating an automatic COPY JOB is to create an S3 event integration. The requirements are:

- **Bucket policy:** The S3 bucket must have a bucket policy allowing s3:GetBucketNotification, s3:PutBucketNotification and s3:GetBucketLocation for the redshift.amazonaws.com principal.
- **Region:** The S3 bucket and the integration must be in the same AWS Region. More generally, the source S3 bucket and the target data warehouse must be in the same AWS Region.
- **IAM role:** The target cluster or serverless namespace must have permission to the bucket via an associated IAM role. The role's policy must allow s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the bucket and its contents, and the role must have a trust relationship allowing redshift.amazonaws.com to assume it.
- **Resource policy:** The Redshift data warehouse must have a resource policy that allows the S3 bucket. This policy authorizes redshift:AuthorizeInboundIntegration and redshift:CreateInboundIntegration.
  - If the target is in the same AWS account as the integration, the console offers a "Fix it for me" option to add the resource policy.
  - If the target is in a different AWS account, the resource policy must be applied to the target manually. The put-resource-policy AWS CLI command can attach a resource policy.

The integration name is a unique identifier across all integrations owned by the AWS account in the current Region. Up to 50 tag keys can be entered for an integration.

## CLI commands

- create-integration takes integration-name, source-arn and target-arn.
- delete-integration deletes an S3 event integration.
- modify-integration changes the name or description of an integration.
- describe-integrations shows properties of an integration.

## Deleting an integration

When an S3 event integration is deleted, the status of the corresponding COPY JOB changes from 1 (active) to 0 (inactive/pending). The COPY JOB is not automatically dropped. Because of this, creating a COPY JOB with the same name as an undropped job might conflict. Amazon Redshift matches the bucket in the COPY JOB CREATE FROM clause to the bucket used in the S3 event integration.

## Limits and considerations

- A maximum of 200 COPY JOBs can be created per cluster or workgroup in an AWS account.
- A maximum of 50 S3 event integrations can be created per Redshift target.
- An S3 event integration cannot be created with a source bucket whose name contains a period.
- Only one S3 event integration can exist between the same source bucket and target.
- The source bucket cannot have existing S3_OBJECT_CREATED event notifications when the integration is created. After an integration is created, however, the bucket event notification can be updated with a narrower prefix/suffix.
- Asia Pacific (New Zealand) does not have auto-copy available.

## Restoring snapshots and recovery points

When a serverless namespace is restored from a snapshot or recovery point to the same namespace, S3 event integrations and their COPY JOBs are maintained automatically. Restoring a snapshot to a different namespace does not maintain S3 event integrations. Snapshot restores on provisioned clusters likewise do not maintain S3 event integrations.

After a restore, Redshift automatically ingests files in S3 that have not yet been loaded and that were uploaded after the snapshot. Files uploaded after the snapshot and deleted before the restore completes are not ingested.

The outcome depends on what changed after the snapshot was taken:

- If an integration was created after the snapshot was taken, the integration enters the NEEDS_ATTENTION state after the restore.
- If an integration was deleted after the snapshot was taken, the integration is not restored and the COPY JOB status changes to PENDING. In this case, files added to S3 between the snapshot time and COPY JOB recreation cannot be recovered or re-ingested.
- If COPY JOBs were changed after the snapshot was taken, the restored namespace uses the COPY JOBs from the snapshot.
- If the user opts out of maintaining integrations during the restore, the integrations enter the FAILED state after the restore.

# Auto-copy from Amazon S3 into Amazon Redshift

## Overview

An auto-copy job loads data into Amazon Redshift tables from files stored in Amazon S3. Amazon Redshift detects new S3 files added to the path specified in the COPY command, and a COPY command is run automatically when new files are detected. Amazon Redshift keeps track of which files have been loaded, and it determines the number of files batched per COPY command. A COPY JOB is defined once, and the same parameters are used for future runs. Defining and managing a COPY JOB requires permission.

## Creating an automatic COPY JOB

The first step to create an automatic COPY JOB is to create an S3 event integration. The following requirements apply:

- The S3 bucket must have a bucket policy allowing s3:GetBucketNotification, s3:PutBucketNotification and s3:GetBucketLocation for the redshift.amazonaws.com principal.
- The source S3 bucket and target data warehouse must be in the same AWS Region, and the S3 bucket and the integration are likewise in the same AWS Region.
- The target cluster or serverless namespace must have permission to the bucket via an associated IAM role. The IAM role policy must allow s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the bucket and its contents, and the role must have a trust relationship allowing redshift.amazonaws.com to assume it.
- The Redshift data warehouse must have a resource policy that allows the S3 bucket. This resource policy authorizes redshift:AuthorizeInboundIntegration and redshift:CreateInboundIntegration. If the target is in the same AWS account as the integration, the console offers a Fix it for me option to add the resource policy. If the target is in a different AWS account, the resource policy must be applied to the target manually. The put-resource-policy AWS CLI command can attach a resource policy.

The integration name is a unique identifier across all integrations owned by the AWS account in the current Region. Up to 50 tag keys can be entered for an integration.

## Managing integrations with the CLI

The create-integration CLI command takes integration-name, source-arn and target-arn. delete-integration deletes an S3 event integration, modify-integration changes the name or description of an integration, and describe-integrations shows properties of an integration.

## Deleting an integration

When an S3 event integration is deleted, the corresponding COPY JOB status changes from 1 (active) to 0 (inactive/pending). The corresponding COPY JOB is not automatically dropped. Creating a COPY JOB with the same name as an undropped job might conflict. Amazon Redshift matches the bucket in the COPY JOB CREATE FROM clause to the bucket used in the S3 event integration.

## Limitations

- A maximum of 200 COPY JOBs can be created per cluster or workgroup in an AWS account.
- A maximum of 50 S3 event integrations can be created per Redshift target.
- An S3 event integration cannot be created with a source bucket whose name contains a period.
- Only one S3 event integration can exist between the same source bucket and target.
- The source bucket cannot have existing S3_OBJECT_CREATED event notifications when the integration is created. After an integration is created, the bucket event notification can be updated with a narrower prefix/suffix.
- Asia Pacific (New Zealand) does not have auto-copy available.

## Snapshot restore behavior

When a serverless namespace is restored from a snapshot or recovery point to the same namespace, S3 event integrations and their COPY JOBs are maintained automatically. Restoring a snapshot to a different namespace does not maintain S3 event integrations. Snapshot restores on provisioned clusters also do not maintain S3 event integrations.

After a restore, Redshift automatically ingests files in S3 not yet loaded that were uploaded after the snapshot. Files uploaded after the snapshot and deleted before restore completes are not ingested.

Several cases depend on what changed after the snapshot was taken:

- If an integration was created after the snapshot was taken, the integration enters the NEEDS_ATTENTION state after restore.
- If an integration was deleted after the snapshot was taken, the integration is not restored and the COPY JOB status changes to PENDING. Files added to S3 between snapshot time and COPY JOB recreation cannot be recovered or re-ingested.
- If COPY JOBs were changed after the snapshot was taken, the restored namespace uses the COPY JOBs from the snapshot.
- If the user opts out of maintaining integrations during restore, integrations enter the FAILED state after the restore.

# Creating an auto-copy job from Amazon S3 to Amazon Redshift

## Before you begin

Complete or confirm each of the following before you create an S3 event integration or a COPY JOB.

- **Target Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster or Redshift Serverless namespace/workgroup.** This is the data warehouse that receives the data.
- **Source Amazon S3 bucket.** It must be in the same AWS Region as the integration and the target, and its name must not contain a period.
- **Bucket policy on the S3 bucket.** It must allow the required Amazon S3 permissions (s3:GetBucketNotification, s3:PutBucketNotification and s3:GetBucketLocation) to the redshift.amazonaws.com principal. Steps are on this page.
- **IAM role associated with the Redshift cluster or serverless namespace.** It must have a trust relationship that allows redshift.amazonaws.com to assume it. Steps are on this page.
- **IAM identity policy on the role.** It must allow s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the bucket and its contents. Steps are on this page.
- **Association of the IAM role with the provisioned cluster.** Steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/copy-unload-iam-role-associating-with-clusters.html.
- **Association of the IAM role with the Redshift Serverless namespace.** Steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/serverless-security-other-services.html.
- **Resource policy on the Redshift data warehouse (cluster or serverless namespace).** It must authorize the S3 bucket/integration source. Steps are on this page.

## How auto-copy works

An auto-copy job loads data into Amazon Redshift tables from files stored in Amazon S3. Amazon Redshift detects new S3 files added to the path specified in the COPY command. A COPY command is run automatically only when new files are detected, so detection must occur first. Amazon Redshift keeps track of which files have been loaded and determines the number of files batched per COPY command.

## Create an S3 event integration

The first step to create an automatic COPY JOB is to create an S3 event integration. This step holds only when all of the following are true:

- The S3 bucket has a bucket policy allowing s3:GetBucketNotification, s3:PutBucketNotification and s3:GetBucketLocation for the redshift.amazonaws.com principal.
- The S3 bucket and the integration are in the same AWS Region. The source S3 bucket and the target data warehouse must be in the same AWS Region, which is enough to satisfy this requirement.
- The target cluster or serverless namespace has permission to the bucket through an associated IAM role.
- The IAM role policy allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the bucket and its contents.
- The IAM role has a trust relationship allowing redshift.amazonaws.com to assume it.
- The Redshift data warehouse has a resource policy that allows the S3 bucket.

The resource policy authorizes redshift:AuthorizeInboundIntegration and redshift:CreateInboundIntegration.

### Adding the resource policy

If the target is in the same AWS account as the integration, the console offers a **Fix it for me** option to add the resource policy. This option is available only when the target is in the same account. If the target is in a different AWS account, the option is not available, so the resource policy must be applied to the target manually. The put-resource-policy AWS CLI command can attach a resource policy.

### Integration settings

The integration name is a unique identifier across all integrations owned by the AWS account in the current Region. You can enter up to 50 tag keys for an integration.

### CLI commands

The create-integration CLI command takes integration-name, source-arn and target-arn. Supplying these is enough to create the integration. Related commands:

- delete-integration deletes an S3 event integration.
- modify-integration changes the name or description of an integration.
- describe-integrations shows properties of an integration.

## Create the COPY JOB

Create the S3 event integration before you create the COPY JOB. Amazon Redshift matches the bucket in the COPY JOB CREATE FROM clause to the bucket used in the S3 event integration. A COPY JOB is defined once, and the same parameters are used for future runs. Defining and managing a COPY JOB requires permission.

## Limits and restrictions

- A maximum of 200 COPY JOBs can be created per cluster or workgroup in an AWS account.
- A maximum of 50 S3 event integrations can be created per Redshift target.
- An S3 event integration cannot be created with a source bucket whose name contains a period.
- Only one S3 event integration can exist between the same source bucket and target.
- The source bucket cannot have existing S3_OBJECT_CREATED event notifications when the integration is created. After an integration is created, the bucket event notification can be updated with a narrower prefix/suffix.
- Asia Pacific (New Zealand) does not have auto-copy available.

## Deleting an integration

When an S3 event integration is deleted, the corresponding COPY JOB status changes from 1 (active) to 0 (inactive/pending). The COPY JOB is not automatically dropped. Creating a COPY JOB with the same name as an undropped job might conflict.

## Snapshot and recovery point restores

When a serverless namespace is restored from a snapshot or recovery point to the same namespace, S3 event integrations and their COPY JOBs are maintained automatically. This maintenance holds only in that case. Restoring a snapshot to a different namespace does not maintain S3 event integrations, and if the user opts out of maintaining integrations during restore, integrations also are not maintained. In that opt-out case, integrations enter the FAILED state after the restore. Snapshot restores on provisioned clusters do not maintain S3 event integrations.

For a same-namespace serverless restore, after restore Redshift automatically ingests files in S3 not yet loaded that were uploaded after the snapshot. Files uploaded after the snapshot and deleted before restore completes are not ingested. The following cases also apply:

- If an integration was created after the snapshot was taken, the integration enters the NEEDS_ATTENTION state after restore.
- If an integration was deleted after the snapshot was taken, the integration is not restored and the COPY JOB status changes to PENDING. Files added to S3 between snapshot time and COPY JOB recreation cannot be recovered or re-ingested.
- If COPY JOBs were changed after the snapshot was taken, the restored namespace uses the COPY JOBs from the snapshot.
